sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: The office originated as the **Agent of the East India Company** for its factories in Bengal, transforming into a political and military authority after Robert Clive secured the **Diwani rights** in 1765.
• **Foundational Principle 2**: The **Dual System of Government in Bengal** (1765-1772) instituted by Robert Clive separated Nizamat (military/criminal justice) from Diwani (revenue administration), creating administrative chaos and rampant corruption.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: Warren Hastings abolished the Dual System in 1772 and brought the administration directly under company control, culminating in his elevation to the first **Governor-General of Bengal** under the Regulating Act of 1773.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The transition of Bengal governance directly mirrors the shift of the British from traders to sovereign rulers of India.

items.definition: The right to collect and administer land revenue of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa granted to the East India Company by Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II in 1765.
Administration of criminal justice and military defense, nominally retained by the Nawab of Bengal under the Dual System.
A corrupt and inefficient administrative mechanism where the Company exercised Diwani functions and the Nawab exercised Nizamat, leading to the devastating Bengal Famine of 1770.
Statutory enactment that redesignated the Governor of Bengal as the 'Governor-General of Bengal' and created an Executive Council of four members to assist him.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Region / Zone Details**: Bengal Presidency encompassing modern-day West Bengal, Bangladesh, Bihar, Odisha, and parts of Assam.
• **Driving Advantages**: Fertile Gangetic plains, massive textile and silk trade hubs, and strategic port access via Calcutta (Fort William).

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Rampant private trade by company officials, severe economic drain, famine, and lack of central accountability.
• **Policy Interventions**: Abolition of Dual System, introduction of professional civil servants, judicial reorganization under Warren Hastings and Cornwallis.

items.title: Mnemonic for Bengal Executive Evolution
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'Clive Dual-ed Hastings Gen-ed' (Clive Dualed, Hastings Generalised).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Clive instituted the **Dual** system -> Warren Hastings became the first **Governor-General**.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly distinguishes between the Governor of Bengal, the Dual System era, and the Governor-General of Bengal.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Plassey (1757) = Political Footprint; Buxar (1764) = Legal Supremacy (Diwani 1765); Regulating Act (1773) = Centralization.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently creates confusion by stating Warren Hastings was the 'First Governor-General of India'. He was the 'First Governor-General of Bengal'. William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India (1833).

Mains Value Addition: Analyze how the office of the Governor of Bengal transitioned from a commercial corporate agent to a sovereign political administrator, laying the bedrock of the British administrative and judicial apparatus in India.

keyTakeaways: The office of the Governor of Bengal was established post-Plassey and solidified via the 1765 Diwani grant.
The Dual System (1765-1772) under Clive caused severe economic exploitation and administrative collapse, culminating in the 1770 famine.
The Regulating Act of 1773 ended the designation of Governor of Bengal, upgrading it to Governor-General of Bengal to centralize control.
